summary.title: Agentic Game Development as a Verifiable Trajectory Data Engine for Scaling World Models

setting_and_object.category: Training paradigm / framework (position paper with pilot studies)

details: World-model / spatial-generation post-training lacks a cheap, grounded verifier: quality is judged by fuzzy, gameable proxies (CLIP, FVD, MLLM-as-judge), so RL post-training cannot compound the way it does for code and math.
Thesis: the bottleneck is the feedback channel, not data or compute; game development already contains the missing verifier.

RLHEV (Reinforcement Learning with Human-Engine Verification): a post-training reward that gates candidates on hard game-engine checks (loading, collision, physics stability, navmesh reachability, bounded playability) and then fuses dense normalized engine reward with the developer's accept/reject acceptance signal, optimized offline as reward-weighted, KL-regularized policy training.
AWoMo (Agentic World Model): a world model embedded in a propose-render-verify-repair-review developer loop with intent/action/verification/review interfaces, whose runs are the training data.

UWDP: a typed multimodal protocol storing each loop as an object-linked state-action-check-review trace (intent, scene program, edit, engine output, rendered evidence, reviewer decision, repair links) instead of only the final artifact.

Neural core 'UnifiedGameAssetModel': 2.89B-parameter Mixture-of-Transformers initialized from Cosmos 3, hidden 3584, 8 layers, 4 heads, 4 gated experts, with modality-typed heads for text, images, meshes, 3D Gaussians, and Unity/Unreal/Godot/MuJoCo representations.

On-policy distillation then continued pretraining on an AWoMo manifest of 87,745 accepted and 504 rejected developer-authorized UWDP records (79,130 train / 4,333 val / 4,282 test), 8 A100 workers, global batch 4096, best checkpoint at step 589.
Binary accept/reject classification of edited Unity asset candidates from edit prompt, Unity asset/context features, reference-image and layout features; 720 train / 80 val / 200 balanced test.
Primary metric = 0.45 balanced accuracy + 0.25 accuracy + 0.20 F1 + 0.10 AUC; 8 seeds; training-budget sweep 40-720 instances plus a generation-side quality evaluation.
Full RLHEV reward weights: 0.65 human + 0.35 engine, applied only after all hard engine gates pass.

Zero-shot CLIP threshold classifier; Fuzzy Proxies Baseline (CLIP-similarity reward); SFT on ground-truth accept/reject labels; Offline RLHF (human reward only, alpha=1,beta=0); Engine-based RLVR (engine reward only, alpha=0,beta=1).

Representation ablation: snapshot-only features (format tags, prompt length, asset count, output size) vs protocol-trace features (Unity accept/reject label, deviation type, target-engine id, asset identity), ridge-regression ranking probes with only 8 labeled target-engine examples.

Distribution transfer Unity to held-out Unity (5,895 source / 1,254 target); cross-engine Unity to Unreal and Godot (1,000 instances each, 720/80/200); conditions: zero-shot, source-only, target-only scratch, target-adapted transfer (160 adaptation steps).
Metric: normalized MLLM-as-a-judge score in [0,1] (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B under the human accept/reject rubric, human-verified, evaluation-only, never a training reward), plus proxy score and loss.

Embodied diagnostics: R2R (SAME/DUET, val-unseen success rate), Gymnasium MuJoCo rollout return, D4RL Gym-MuJoCo normalized score; AWoMo used as a profile-guided data-augmentation/filtering workflow, compared to original and naive augmentation baselines.

key_findings.finding: Fusing human acceptance with engine checks beats either signal alone and beats fuzzy-proxy and supervised training on both understanding and generation of Unity assets.
key_findings.evidence: On UnitySceneBench (best-of-eight seeds, 720 training instances) Full RLHEV reaches 0.681 primary score, 0.665 accuracy/balanced accuracy, 0.733 F1, 0.690 AUC, exceeding the strongest non-full baseline by +0.098 primary and +0.120 accuracy; on the generation side it reaches 0.8197 mean quality at 720 instances versus 0.7934 for Engine-based RLVR, and dominates Offline RLHF, SFT and fuzzy-proxy baselines at every training budget from 40 to 720.

key_findings.finding: Development traces carry far more transferable supervision than final-artifact snapshots, supporting the paper's central data-engine claim.
key_findings.evidence: With only 8 labeled target-engine examples, protocol-trace features reach 0.719+/-0.094 held-out Spearman correlation with target-engine pass/warn labels versus 0.159+/-0.168 for snapshot-only features (0.758 vs 0.141 with 720 source instances); the trace advantage of ~0.56-0.62 is far larger than the gain from scaling source instances.

key_findings.finding: Pretraining on human-engine-verified source traces yields positive OOD and cross-engine transfer after target adaptation.
key_findings.evidence: MLLM-judge score on the Unity distribution shift rises from 0.25 (target-only scratch) to 0.75 with source pretraining plus target adaptation; Unity-to-Unreal rises 0.25 to 0.35 and Unity-to-Godot 0.15 to 0.35, with higher proxy scores (0.474/0.478 vs 0.437/0.441) and lower loss; source-only checkpoints without target adaptation degrade badly (judge 0.15, loss ~16.7).

key_findings.finding: Environment data generated by the AWoMo workflow improves downstream embodied policies over both original and naive-augmentation training.
key_findings.evidence: Direction-normalized gains over the original baseline: +0.79% R2R success rate (76.607 vs 76.006), +9.96% Gymnasium MuJoCo rollout return (1724.73 vs 1568.44), and +48.43% D4RL Gym-MuJoCo normalized score (27.155 vs 18.295), with AWoMo best on all three and ahead of naive augmentation.

key_findings.finding: The evidence is explicitly diagnostic and bounded, with engine reward acknowledged as a partial, gameable verifier.
key_findings.evidence: Experiments use small splits (200-example test sets, headline table reported best-of-eight seeds), no real scans, robots, or real-to-sim-to-real loop; the paper states the claims do not imply final game quality or human-preference alignment, and prescribes verifier ensembles, randomized probes, held-out checks and human review to counter engine reward hacking.
